season.evidence: Stored May-Oct kept. Logged Kamikaze ascents cluster Jan-Jul and Aug-Oct with a spring peak; WebSearch of WTA trip reports shows the upper Kamikaze line holding snow/ice Dec-Apr and snow-free by late spring through fall; Mountaineers lists a separate winter scramble, so May-Oct is the clear-ground window.

track.why: Logged route 'Kamikaze Route' (Aug 20 2020), summited, round trip from the Teneriffe trailhead (start/end within 47 m of our pin, summit 2 m from ours). Report describes the falls viewpoint, steep rooty switchbacks, rocky ridge, bracken clearing above 4000 ft then joining the main trail for the summit rocks - exactly our Kamikaze line; stats show descent by the standard route, i.e. our ~10 mile loop.

facts.text: Where the forest path splits into several faint lines, stay on the crest of the ridge and the boot track reappears.
Past about 4,000 ft the track crosses a bracken-and-fireweed clearing and a short rocky outcrop of easy scrambling before it joins the standard trail for the last summit rocks.
By late May, continuous slushy snow covers the route above roughly 4,300 ft, and the lower tread can stay packed snow down toward 3,800 ft.
The trailhead gate was reported locked at about 8 pm and unlocked around 7 am in May and August, so plan a loop that finishes before then.

season.evidence: Stored Mar-Nov; WebSearch of WTA trip reports shows continuous snow on the upper ridge in Mar-early May, melted out late spring to fall, snow returning by Nov-Dec; logged standard-trail ascents are spread across the year with a Jan-May bulge from snow-free lower trail. Kept the stored breadth but report snow-free best Jun-Oct.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Every harvested track with geometry leaves the trail for the Teneriffe Falls / Kamikaze boot track (passes within 80 m of our Kamikaze junction pin); none ascends the standard switchback trail and returns. The standard-trail reports (1210875 Aug 2019, 2507257 May 2024, 288440 Oct 2011) have no track points.
Kamikaze up / standard down loop; filed under the Kamikaze route, not assigned twice.

facts.text: A small false summit knob sits in the trees about half a mile short of the top; keep going past it.
In early May snow patches begin near 3,850 ft and become continuous by about 4,000 ft, covering most of the final stretch along the ridge.
The trailhead gate was reported locked at about 8 pm and unlocked around 7 am in May and August, so budget the descent to beat it.

notes: Standard route got no track: all harvested geometry uses the falls/Kamikaze line, and the standard-only reports carry no GPS. The stored Teneriffe-area routes are distinct lines (Kamikaze boot track vs graded switchbacks); no duplicates detected.
